audit.why: FAV 6/10 at 52.73% over 1210 games is right — Riven owns the whole laning phase and only loses the game state once Mundo has two items.
audit.corrected: Rating kept; the chart rows corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 and Levels 4-5 and Level 6 were all Skill while the prose says Mundo is 'a free punching bag' at 1 and Level 6 is 'your hardest decisive window all game'; meanwhile First item and 2+ items were credited to Riven though whys[6] says a Warmog's Mundo is unkillable.
audit.why: The mirror audit has already shipped Riven for levels 1 through 6, Skill at first item and Dr. Mundo at two items. The prose on this page supports that order exactly; the shipped chart argued against its own text in five rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4, 5 and 6 flipped as matched full/content pairs with ratings realigned, and the phases whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page builds the entire Level 2 and Level 3 gameplan on landing Ki Burst, and never mentions that Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilising effect that hits him.
audit.why: Mundo's passive eats your first stun outright — he loses health and drops a cannister instead of being stunned, and picking it up heals him and lowers the passive's cooldown. Ki Burst is the only immobilise in Riven's kit, so this single interaction decides every all-in in the lane, and a player following the current text will commit a full chain into a stun that simply does not land.
audit.corrected: whys[1] and wants.you[1] now treat the first Ki Burst as a bait for the passive, with the second stun as the real one. Blunt Force Trauma is also an auto-attack reset, so his damage opens on a wind-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] and mid both tell you to engage 'when his cleaver is on cooldown'.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4-second cooldown. There is no window to wait for — the advice is unusable and would have a player standing in poke range waiting for something that is always back.
audit.corrected: Both restated around the 4s figure: you cannot wait it out, you close behind minions instead.

audit.why: Early Executioner's Calling and permanent Grievous Wounds are correct and already stated in wants.you[2], spikes[3] and late — Maximum Dosage heals a percentage of missing health, so resistances are the wrong lever and anti-heal is the right one.

edits.before: Your Q resets win level 1 if you weave autos between casts. Identify how Dr. Mundo contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mundo has no CC and no escape at Level 1 — his only tool is a max-range cleaver, so step up, weave Runic Blade autos and deny him CS.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Heart Zapper's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4s, so there is no window to wait for — close behind minions, keep him under threat, and bank the lead.

edits.before: Blade of the Exile + the wind-slash execute turns half-HP fights lethal. Reassess every all-in at 6 â€” Dr. Mundo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile into Wind Slash is your hardest window all game — force it before he recalls for Warmog's, and hold Grievous Wounds on him.

edits.before: Eclipse is your spike â€” force fights the moment it completes, on Heart Zapper's cooldown.
edits.after: Your Eclipse and his Heartsteel land together — cash the lead now, not in a later fight.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Dr. Mundo carry threat 8/10 â€” close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Warmog's and Maximum Dosage refill him between every fight — the side lane is his now, so take your objectives elsewhere.

edits.before: W unlocks your first real all-in: E forward, Q-auto chain into W stun before he can cleaver you back to range — Mundo's passive regen is too slow to matter inside this window.
edits.after: W unlocks your first real all-in, but his passive resists the first immobilise and drops a cannister instead — so your opening Ki Burst is a bait and the second one is the stun that lands.

edits.before: Infected Bonesaw ranks up and his percent-HP poke becomes a genuine threat to your HP bar — respect max range and engage only when his cleaver is on cooldown rather than forcing every wave.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw ranks up and its current-health damage chunks you, but it is a flat 4-second cooldown — you cannot wait it out, so close the gap behind minions instead of trading at range.

edits.before: Land W stun during the Q chain while Mundo is in your face — without lockdown his passive shrugs the damage and he just walks away
edits.after: Spend an early Ki Burst to strip his passive — it eats your first immobilise outright, so only the second stun actually holds him

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a maintenance window — Mundo's Infected Bonesaw starts hitting meaningful percent-HP chunks as he ranks it up, so respect the max-range cleaver and do not let him whittle you below the all-in threshold before you engage. Your job is to keep him under threat: shove the wave, deny CS, and look for the trade when his Q is on cooldown. At Level 6 Blade of the Exile is your hardest decisive window all game. R-empowered Q chain into W stun into Wind Slash at low HP executes him cleanly, and he has no answer if you hit all three Q segments. Force this before he recalls to buy Warmog's, because every second you wait is gold toward a passive-regen machine you cannot run down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a maintenance window — Infected Bonesaw chunks a share of your current health as he ranks it up, and at a flat 4-second cooldown there is no downtime to wait for, so close behind the minion wave rather than trading at his range. Keep him under threat: shove, deny CS, and step on him when he walks up for a last hit. At Level 6 Blade of the Exile is your hardest decisive window all game. The R-empowered Q chain into Ki Burst into Wind Slash executes him, provided you have already stripped his passive with an earlier stun. Force it before he recalls for Warmog's.

notes: The single most important interaction in this lane was absent: Goes Where He Pleases resists the FIRST immobilising effect, so the opening Ki Burst never stuns — it strips the passive and he drops a cannister that heals him when collected. Every all-in instruction on the page assumed the first stun lands. Chart set to the order the mirror already shipped (Riven through Level 6, Skill at first item, Dr. Mundo at 2+), which differs from packet.levelChart on rows 2, 3 and 4; the mirror wins to keep the pair consistent, and this page's own prose backs it. Infected Bonesaw's flat 4s cooldown made two 'wait for his Q' instructions unusable.
